title: Petra and the Trail
premise: Petra Quintana, a bush pilot hauling medicine and gossip across the Cordillera del Silencio, is the last person to see a government survey team before they vanish from a high valley, leaving their gear stacked and no tracks in or out. When officials decide Petra's silence is worth more than her testimony, she realizes the surveyors stumbled onto something the state wants buried: an old mine whose deeds were stolen from families like hers a generation ago. Grounded by a sabotaged engine and hunted by men who answer to no one, Petra joins forces with Marisol, the daughter of one missing surveyor, and Tomás, an aging guide who remembers where the original land grants were hidden. Crossing the range ahead of the first snows, they follow a trail of cairns and half-buried documents toward the truth—and discover the survey team alive but trapped, held by a former magistrate who has spent thirty years guarding the inheritance he once helped steal. In the end Petra must choose between flying out with proof that could restore the land to its rightful heirs and staying to carry the injured to safety; she does both, burning her own debt note as the price of passage, and the mountains keep what remains.
about_author: Dominic Whitlock is a former charter pilot who logged a decade of flights over remote mountain ranges before turning to fiction full-time. He writes adventure novels about people who live where maps run out, drawing on his own close calls with weather, machinery, and silence.

chapters.title: Fuel and Rumor
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She flies her routine circuit—medicine, mail, gossip—into the interior, establishing her debts, her compass, and her careful habit of not asking questions. At a mission airstrip she hears the survey team mentioned for the first time. Emotional beat: restless competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Last Drop
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She makes an unscheduled supply drop at the survey camp in a high valley, exchanging brief words with the team leader, Elena Vasco, who presses a folded paper into Petra's map case 'for later.' Weather closes in behind her. Emotional beat: unease she can't name.

chapters.title: Gear Without Tracks
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Ten days later, returning on schedule, she finds the camp intact—tents pitched, stove warm, gear stacked—but no people and no tracks leaving. The folded paper turns out to be a fragment of an old land deed. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Questions in the Capital
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with a shift to an official's memo. In town, bureaucrats question her closely, more interested in what she saw than in finding anyone. A stranger photographs her plane. She realizes her testimony is a liability. Emotional beat: the hunter becoming the hunted.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Her engine fails on takeoff; she crash-lands on a riverbar, walking away with bruises and a dead aircraft. The mechanic finds grit in the fuel line. Staying invisible was never an option. Emotional beat: fury transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: Marisol
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Elena Vasco's daughter arrives looking for her mother, armed with stubbornness and a second copy of the deed fragment. She and Petra compare papers: the deeds match a mine worked by Petra's grandfather before his claim was seized. Emotional beat: two griefs recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Tomás Remembers
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. An old guide who once carried ore from the mine tells them the original grant documents were hidden in a shrine above the tree line when the seizures began. He agrees to lead them—for reasons he won't explain. Emotional beat: guilt finally given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: The Men Who Answer to No One
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Armed riders burn the mission airstrip where Petra refueled, asking after 'the pilot who landed at the empty camp.' The trio slips into the forest as the search widens. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into discipline.

chapters.title: Cairns
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Above the tree line they find stone cairns too regular to be natural—a trail marker system predating the survey, built by hands that knew the route. Someone has walked this way recently. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: The Shrine
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. They reach the ruined shrine and dig out a tin box: complete land grants, names of forty families, and a ledger of payments made to officials—including a signature belonging to a magistrate declared dead years ago. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden, not gift.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. First snows arrive early. Tomás confesses he helped seize the claims as a young man and has been paying for it ever since; the magistrate, Aurelio Sanch, was his brother-in-law. Emotional beat: confession as release and risk.

chapters.title: The Pass That Isn't
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Their mapped pass is blocked by a rockslide—recently triggered. They are being funneled. Petra spots smoke from a fire that shouldn't exist and chooses to walk toward it. Emotional beat: courage as a decision, not a feeling.

chapters.title: The Living
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. They find three of the survey team alive in a cave, weak but breathing, including Elena. The others died in a fall the team covered up while waiting for rescue that never came. Elena reveals why they hid: they found the mine and the ledgers, and someone wanted them gone. Emotional beat: reunion shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: The Magistrate
chapters.summary: Elena's POV (interleaved flashback). Years ago, Aurelio Sanch faked his death rather than face reckoning for the forged seizures, and has lived above the snowline since, watching the mine, keeping the secret like a wound. Now he has found them. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Sanch confronts them—not with violence but with a bargain: the documents in exchange for the survivors' safe passage down, because he cannot carry them himself and winter will kill everyone. Petra doesn't trust him. Emotional beat: negotiation at the edge of exhaustion.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Keeps
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. A storm pins them all together in the cave for two days. Sanch and Tomás reckon with each other across thirty years of silence. Sanch admits the deeds were never legally destroyed—only hidden—meaning the families' claim still stands. Emotional beat: justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Storm breaks; they begin carrying the injured down the far side, Sanch guiding them through routes only he knows. One stretcher party is nearly lost in a whiteout; Sanch saves them at real personal risk. Emotional beat: trust built in motion.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Riverbar
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. At the riverbar, the armed riders are waiting—they've been tracking Sanch, their paymaster's loose end. Sanch offers himself in exchange for letting the others go. Petra refuses to accept the trade. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Flight
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra repairs her plane with parts cannibalized from the wrecked supply cache, improvising under fire. She gets Elena, Marisol, and the deed box airborne as the riders reach the bar. Emotional beat: everything riding on one engine.

chapters.title: Debt Paid
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Landing at the capital strip, Petra learns her own family's debt note—the leverage used against her—has been bought by the same men. She burns it publicly, choosing exposure over safety, and hands the deeds to a judge with nothing left to lose. Emotional beat: freedom purchased with visibility.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Hearings begin; forty families file claims under the recovered grants. Sanch surrenders voluntarily, testifying to the forgeries, and Tomás stands beside him. Some justice arrives; some never will. Emotional beat: justice as imperfect, human work.

chapters.title: Compass Pointing Home
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, epilogue. Spring. Petra flies her circuit again, now carrying legal papers instead of rumors. Over the high valley she drops a wreath for the surveyors who didn't come back, then banks south toward home. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
